row: Which account is increased by a credit?
Revenue, liabilities and equity increase with credits.
How is a purchase of supplies on credit recorded?
An asset increases and a liability increases.
A balanced trial balance means what?
Total debits = total credits, but errors may still exist
Some errors, such as omitting an entire transaction, do not unbalance the trial balance.
It measures the share of assets financed by debt.
Which error will make the trial balance totals unequal?
A $500 debit to Cash posted as $50
An entire journal entry not posted
A debit posted to the wrong expense account
Only one side changed, so debits ≠ credits. The other errors keep debits equal to credits.
The trial balance debit and credit totals differ by $270. Which error is most likely?
A debit posted to the wrong account
A difference evenly divisible by 9 (270 ÷ 9 = 30) suggests a transposition or slide error.
A $300 payment on account was debited to Accounts Receivable instead of Accounts Payable. Effect?
Trial balance still balances; A/R and A/P both overstated by $300
Trial balance out of balance by $300
Trial balance out of balance by $600
Debits still equal credits. A/R is wrongly increased and A/P was not decreased.
A $800 collection from a customer on account was recorded: Dr Cash 800, Cr Service Revenue 800. Correcting entry?
Dr Service Revenue 800, Cr Accounts Receivable 800
Dr Accounts Receivable 800, Cr Service Revenue 800
Cash is correct. Remove the revenue and reduce Accounts Receivable instead.
Equipment bought for $2,000 cash was recorded: Dr Supplies 2,000, Cr Cash 2,000. Correcting entry?
Cash is correct. Move the $2,000 out of Supplies into Equipment.
A $450 payment to a creditor was recorded: Dr Accounts Payable 540, Cr Cash 540. Correcting entry?
Both accounts were reduced by $90 too much (540 − 450), so add $90 back to each.
